Convert a detset to the four tables of actel::preload()

Source: R/to_actel.R
to_actel.Rd

Returns biometrics, spatial, deployments and detections in the forms actel 1.4.0 reads, so that do.call(actel::preload, c(to_actel(x, tz), list(tz = tz))) runs.

Usage

to_actel(x, tz, arrays = NULL)

Arguments

x

A detset with an animals table.

tz

The study area's time zone, from OlsonNames().

arrays

Optional named character vector: the actel array of each station, named by station_id.

Value

A list of four data frames: biometrics, spatial, deployments and detections, with the attributes receivers, open_deployments, deployments, dropped, dropped_animals, actel_drops and shared_code_unheard.

Details

Time. actel reads detections in UTC and converts them to the study area's time zone, but reads release and deployment times as already in that zone. So detections$Timestamp stays in UTC, while biometrics$Release.date and the deployments' Start and Stop are the same instants shown in tz. Give preload() the same tz.

Arrays. actel places stations in arrays joined by a graph, which suits rivers and gates. A lake array has none, so by default every station is in array "A1"; give arrays, a named vector of array codes by station_id, to set your own, and the matching dot to preload(). Every row of spatial is in section "All", the section actel gives a spatial table that names none.

Receivers. actel names a receiver by a whole number. Each distinct receiver_serial gets its own: the serial itself where it is all digits once a model prefix such as "VR2Tx-" is dropped and no other receiver shares it, and a new number above every serial otherwise, as for OTN names such as "HFX047-250049-2" or "144(lost/found)". The attribute receivers holds the lookup (Receiver, receiver_serial, receiver_model); give it to read_detset_from() to restore the names.

Sensors. A calibrated reading goes out as Sensor.Value with its unit. A raw reading with no calibration goes out as Sensor.Value with Sensor.Unit "ADC", as GLATOS exports write it, so the way back puts it in sensor_raw again.

Deployments. actel needs a Stop time for every deployment and stops on a receiver whose deployments overlap, so the deployments are bounded as to_ato() bounds them (see there): an open deployment ends at the next deployment of its receiver, or one second after the last detection; a deployment that runs past the next one of its receiver ends where that one starts; and only the deployments that overlap the detections, from the first to the last, are exported. The attribute deployments counts each kind, and a warning gives the counts when a deployment was trimmed or left out. spatial lists the stations of the exported deployments.

Rows left out. Detections with no station_id match no deployment in actel and are left out, as are detections whose code cannot be read; the attribute dropped counts them by reason, and a warning gives the total. An animal whose transmitter has no acoustic code space, such as a satellite tag in an OTN tag release file, is left out of biometrics; the attribute dropped_animals counts them, and a warning names one. actel::preload() itself then drops the detections of transmitters that are not in biometrics and those before their animal's release. The attribute actel_drops counts both ahead of time, and a warning gives the total, so the loss is on record before actel makes it.

Animals. Biometrics have one row per animal, with its transmitters' IDs in Signal joined by |, as actel reads tags with several codes, and animal_id kept as an extra column. When no animal has two codes, Signal is an integer, as actel requires. An animal whose codes lie in two code spaces has one row per code space, because actel reads one code space per row; a warning counts them. actel reads one animal per transmitter, so a transmitter reused on a second animal stops to_actel(), unless all but one of the animals that share it have no detection in the set: those are left out of biometrics, a message counts them, and the attribute shared_code_unheard names them. Release sites come from the release positions in the animals table; without them actel puts every animal at one unspecified site. When some animals have a release position and others none, spatial gains a release row named "unspecified" with no position, which actel needs for the animals it puts there, and a warning counts those animals.

See also

read_detset_from() for the way back.

Examples

study <- detqc_example
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
actel_input <- to_actel(dets, tz = "America/Toronto")
lapply(actel_input, nrow)
#> $biometrics
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $spatial
#> [1] 21
#> 
#> $deployments
#> [1] 20
#> 
#> $detections
#> [1] 3297
#> 
head(actel_input$biometrics)
#>          Release.date Signal Code.space   Group Release.site animal_id
#> 1 2024-06-02 11:30:00  61001   A69-1601 walleye           R1     ST-01
#> 2 2024-06-02 11:30:00  61002   A69-9002 walleye           R1     ST-02
#> 3 2024-06-02 11:30:00  61003   A69-9002 walleye           R1     ST-03
#> 4 2024-06-02 11:30:00  61004   A69-1601 walleye           R1     ST-04
